about: The epistle of the Fourth Sunday of Advent. Paul takes the verdict away from the Corinthians and from himself alike — it belongs to the Lord, and it is not given until He comes.

s01.translation: Brethren: Let people regard us as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s02.translation: What is required of stewards is that each be found faithful.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s03.translation: It matters very little to me whether I am judged by you or by a human court; I do not even judge myself.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s04.translation: For I am not conscious of anything against myself, yet this does not justify me; the Lord is the One who judges me.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s05.translation: Therefore do not judge before the time, until the Lord comes. He will bring to light the things hidden in darkness and reveal the counsels of hearts; then each will receive praise from God.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

w025.function: An adjective used as a noun: “a very small thing”. It is the superlative of parvus.

w033.function: Day in the sense of a court sitting, as in the day of the Lord. The Greek behind it says a human day, that is, a human tribunal.

w067.function: A plural participle used as a noun: the hidden things.
